problem: Existing VLN models treat STOP like any other action, so in urban navigation (Touchdown) agents often pass or stop short of the goal even when on the right path, since STOP is rare (once per episode) and irreversible.
motivation: A wrong stop ends the episode with no chance to recover, and STOP needs different reasoning (instruction completeness, matching target to scene) than choosing directions. Oracle experiments show wrong stopping is the main bottleneck.
key_idea: Split the policy into a Stop Indicator (binary stop/non-stop, trained with an up-weighted stop loss) and a Direction Decider that chooses turns only at intersections (key points).
insight: Ablation: removing the loss weighting hurts most (TC 19.48 -> 12.65), so class imbalance of STOP is the main issue; removing the two-branch design gives 15.40 and removing key points gives 15.18. Oracle Stop raises TC to 61.04 vs 30.63 for Oracle Direction, so stopping remains the main bottleneck. Sharing the encoder and decoder between branches works best, so the stop branch benefits from information in the direction branch.
method: Encoders: CNN visual encoder, bi-LSTM text encoder with soft attention, and an LSTM trajectory encoder produce hidden state h_t (based on the RConcat baseline with added instruction attention, called ARC).
Stop Indicator: a linear layer + softmax over [h_t, time embedding] gives stop/non-stop probabilities; if stop is chosen, the episode ends.
Direction Decider: a linear layer + softmax over {forward, left, right}, activated only at key points (nodes with more than two neighbors); the agent goes forward otherwise.
Weighted stop loss: cross-entropy where the stop signal is weighted by lambda (best 20), so the rare STOP class gets more attention.
Joint loss: gamma*L_direction + (1-gamma)*L_stop with gamma=0.6, trained with teacher forcing.
Shared Enc-Dec: both branches share encoders and trajectory decoder (best of four tested structures).

setting.backbone: CNN + bi-LSTM + LSTM trajectory encoder (ARC + L2Stop), trained from scratch
setting.training_data: Touchdown training set (6,526 examples); no extra data
setting.observation: street-view panorama images (visual features) + instruction text
setting.action_space: discrete: forward, turn left, turn right, stop on a street-view graph

numbers_note: Touchdown is not in the canonical benchmark list, so the names are entered as they appear in the paper. The paper's split is called 'development'; it is entered as 'val'.
results: ARC + L2Stop reaches test TC 16.68, SED 16.34, CLS 53.50 and SDTW 16.34, beating the best baseline RConcat (test SED 9.45) and ARC (13.62). It also improves GA and RConcat when plugged in, showing it is model-agnostic.
limitations: Wrong-stop errors remain the bottleneck: Oracle Stop gives TC 61.04 vs 19.48.
Only evaluated on Touchdown with small models trained from scratch; the key-point assumption relies on the street-graph structure.
Absolute performance is still low (TC under 20%).
